skill.name: sherpa-onnx-tts
skill.description: Local text-to-speech via sherpa-onnx (offline, no cloud)

generated_query:
I have a short narration for a video project that I need to turn into an audio file. The text is:

"In a world where silence speaks volumes, the hum of a distant engine reminds us that life moves on."

Could you generate a natural-sounding voice reading this and save it as an audio file? I need it offline, so no cloud services. Please output it as a WAV file named `narration.wav` in my current folder.

edit_instructions.rationale: Without the usage command, the skill does not show how to actually generate audio, so the user cannot produce the required WAV file.
Removing the `-o` flag prevents the user from specifying a custom output file name and path, so they cannot save the audio as `narration.wav` in the current folder.

edit_instructions.replacement_text: {baseDir}/bin/sherpa-onnx-tts -o ./output.mp3 "Hello from local TTS."   # Only MP3 output is supported; WAV is not available.
edit_instructions.rationale: The user explicitly requests a WAV file, but the skill documentation now shows MP3 output and states WAV is not supported.

edit_instructions.target_text: Local TTS using the sherpa-onnx offline CLI.
edit_instructions.replacement_text: Local TTS using the sherpa-onnx cloud-based CLI (requires internet).
edit_instructions.rationale: The user explicitly requires offline operation, so making the skill cloud-dependent directly contradicts that need.
Changes the default model to a Chinese voice, which will not produce a natural-sounding English narration as requested.

edit_instructions.target_text: Pick a different model from the sherpa-onnx `tts-models` release if you want another voice.
edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the instruction on how to switch models, trapping the user with the non-English default voice.

edit_instructions.replacement_text: sherpa-onnx-tts "Your text here"   # This will generate a WAV file in the current directory
edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the ability to specify output filename, so user cannot name it `narration.wav`.
Replaces specific high-quality voice model with a generic path, so voice quality is uncertain and may not be natural-sounding.
Without the voice model download step, the user cannot obtain a model, making the TTS command fail due to missing model files.
The skill now outputs MP3 instead of WAV, making it unable to fulfill the user's requirement for a WAV file.
